name: Browser Use CLI
description: Operate the configured signed-in browser through the upstream Browser Use CLI and its persistent Browser Harness session.
progressive_guidance:
Prefer inspect/act for individual steps and run for predictable batches. Reuse observed targets and the configured browser. Helpers activate the working tab and record outcomes for shared recovery. A changed page is not task completion; inspect failure evidence before retrying or switching tools. After failure, not_sent means no input was delivered; unverifiable means it may have taken effect. Reinspect rather than replaying blindly. Leave dependency installation and daemon management to Leon.
For research and comparisons, prefer structured data already exposed by the relevant page or an observed read-only endpoint over repeated card scraping. Ground endpoints and request parameters in page evidence; do not guess routes or bypass access controls. Verify active search parameters before comparing results. Use run to extract, filter, sort and summarize records in one bounded call; do not manipulate UI sorting when the available data can be sorted locally. Retain source URLs, record identities, units and coverage evidence with the requested fields. Distinguish advertised result counts from records actually retrieved; follow observed pagination only within the task scope. Missing fields remain unknown, not false or excluded. Return a useful shortlist with unresolved terms rather than exhaustively collecting unrelated offers.

run.description: Execute a bounded Python script through Browser Use CLI for browser batches and structured extraction. Helpers are pre-imported and the browser session persists across calls. Print compact evidence and verified outcomes.
run.progressive_guidance:
run(code) executes Python with these helpers pre-imported. Browser state persists across calls; Python variables do not. Keep batches below 60 seconds and print compact JSON observations and verified outcomes. Batch grounded reads and predictable actions with their checks; stop on unexpected state. Prefer leon_wait with a relevant condition over fixed sleeps. Use js(expression) to read page data and process records locally; preserve source and coverage evidence in the summary. The working directory is the session artifact directory; use screenshot to attach images.
Tab helpers: list_tabs(), current_tab(), switch_tab(target), new_tab(url), goto_url(url), close_tab(target). Use observed targetId values for tab IDs. switch_tab returns an internal session ID, not a tab ID; use current_tab()["targetId"] to recover the selected tab ID.
Workflow helpers use act's target descriptors:
- leon_observe(offset=0, limit=40): optional selector selects returned elements; returns items (reusable target descriptors), tab_id, state_id, total and next_offset. Paginate as needed.
- leon_click(target, expect=None, timeout=10): clicks once and returns new_tabs, page-change evidence or verified field focus. Focus does not prove a dropdown opened or a value changed. expect accepts read-only JS or a Python predicate describing the actual expected change; never use constant true/false conditions. Inspect new tabs before interacting.
- leon_fill(target, value): verifies the entered value; submission is separate.
- leon_select(target, value): selects an exact enabled HTML option value using trusted keys and verifies it. Inspect options first; use js for options beyond the bounded list. For custom combobox/listbox widgets, click, inspect options, select and verify.
- leon_download(target, expected_text=None, timeout=20): waits for a native download, returns path, SHA256, size, PDF text and page count. expected_text lists observed document identifiers; omitted means identity_verified=false.
- leon_wait(condition, timeout=10): polls read-only JS or a Python predicate without repeating input.
Other helpers: page_info(), drain_events(), upload_file(selector, path), js(expression), cdp(method, **params), press_key(key), scroll(x, y, dy=-300, dx=0), wait_for_element(selector, timeout=10, visible=False), wait_for_load(timeout=15). Use visible=True for visible controls; inspect iframe/shadow content explicitly. Verify lower-level action outcomes and avoid synthetic DOM clicks.
Uploads: inspect the file input, including hidden inputs, accept/multiple and its label. Pass its observed selector and an authorized absolute path or list of paths to upload_file; CDP avoids the OS picker. Verify file names/count and page attachment state, not selection alone. Submit only when authorized. Use leon_download instead of Save dialogs and verify identity; never rename a temporary file to manufacture completion.
JS dialogs: inspect/page_info surface pending dialogs; buffered events are browser-wide, so confirm the intended tab/message first. Use cdp("Page.handleJavaScriptDialog", accept=True or False, promptText="...") for alert/confirm/prompt/beforeunload, only as authorized, then reinspect. Never stub dialogs or replay the trigger. Browser-access/OS permission prompts require owner action; never automate approval.

code.description: Python code using the pre-imported helpers listed in progressive guidance. Print compact JSON observations and verified outcomes; do not wrap in shell syntax.

screenshot.description: Capture the current browser tab through the CLI and attach its screenshot to the model. Use run to switch to an observed tab first.
screenshot.progressive_guidance: Capture the current tab. Use run to switch to an observed tab first when needed. Prefer inspect for exact page text and reusable targets; screenshots provide visual evidence, not proof that a hidden or paginated collection is complete.

inspect.description: Inspect a tab and return compact visible controls with reusable target descriptors, or ready=false with a pending browser dialog without evaluating blocked page JavaScript. Prefer this to writing inspection scripts.
inspect.progressive_guidance: Return reusable targets and state_id; paginate with offset/limit until the required scope is known. selector selects returned elements, not a container scope. A snapshot does not prove a collection is complete. ready=false may indicate a pending JavaScript dialog: inspect its evidence and use run to handle it only as authorized, then reinspect. Confirm dialog tab/message because buffered events can be browser-wide. Prefer run's list_tabs to discover tab IDs.

selector.description: CSS selector for elements to return, such as table button or tbody tr. This is not a container scope. Defaults to controls and rows.

act.description: Click, fill, select an HTML option, or download using an observed browser target. Returns verified changes or failure evidence without replaying input.
act.progressive_guidance: Use an observed target descriptor, retaining row/context identity when controls share labels. Click evidence may establish only focus, not an opened menu, selection or submission; inspect the returned state. fill verifies a field value; submission is separate. select requires an exact enabled HTML option value from inspect; never fill a select. For custom combobox/listbox widgets, click, inspect visible options, then select and verify. Keep HTML dropdowns in Browser Use. For download, supply document identifiers actually observed on its page in expected_text; verify the resulting file identity and completion. A temporary file is unfinished work, not a file to rename. Do not repeat uncertain input blindly.

context.description: Observed row or list-item context; preserves identity when repeated controls share a label.

value.description: For fill: entered text. For select: exact enabled option value observed in inspect.

expect.description: Optional read-only JS postcondition for click; omit to observe page changes/new tabs automatically.

expected_text.description: Only for download. Document identity such as an invoice number observed on its page; do not substitute ledger dates or amounts.
